text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-U.N. Secretary-General Annan recommended a six-month renewal, until July 31, of the U.N. peacekeeping force in southern Lebanon.
-Prime Minister Hariri said: "The entire world wants peace and Israel tries to blow it up".
-Syrian Foreign Minister Shara said: "Israel did not succeed in using Lebanon as a mine field and it will not".
-Employees of the national air carrier Middle East Airlines will go on strike today to protest against the company's refusal to meet their pay demands.
-PM Hariri and his Syrian counterpart Zu'bi signed the resolutions adopted by the high Lebanese-Syrian Committee.
-Lebanon's weekly treasury bill issue of January 16 raised 516.6 billion Lebanese pounds.
-Shares in Banque Audi were traded for the first time on the Beirut Stock Exchange at $15 on turnover of 10,000 shares.
-Former prime minister Hoss called for the formation of a parliamentary committee to investigate corruption accusations exchanged by top officials.
-Palestinian refugees held a sit-in outside the offices of U.N. Refugees' Welfare Agency (UNRWA) in south Lebanon camps to protest against the agency's social policies.
-An investigative judge ordered the release on bail of three Iraqi diplomats suspected of involvement in the 1994 murder of an Iraqi opposition figure in Beirut.
